title: 花非花
titleEn: A Flower, Yet Not a Flower
author: 白居易
intro: A riddle with no answer: something that is like a flower and like mist, comes at midnight and leaves at dawn, as brief as a spring dream. Readers have argued for a thousand years about what it is.
analysis: 这首诗很短，却像一个谜语。“花非花，雾非雾”：它像花又不是花，像雾又不是雾。“夜半来，天明去”：半夜来，天一亮就走了。后两句用两个比喻：来的时候像春天的梦，能有多久呢？走的时候像早上的云，再也找不到了。诗人始终没说“它”是什么，所以后人有很多猜测：有人说是夜里的露水或霜，有人说是一段短暂的爱情，有人说是人生中一切美好又留不住的东西。“朝云”还让人想到古代巫山神女“早上是云，晚上是雨”的传说，所以很多人把它读成爱情诗。全诗三字句和七字句交替，节奏轻快，像一首歌，后来还变成了一个词牌名。它的魅力就在“说不清”：每个读者都能放进自己心里那件留不住的事。
analysisEn: This poem is tiny, and it reads like a riddle. “A flower, yet not a flower; mist, yet not mist” — it resembles both, but is neither. “It comes at midnight and leaves at daybreak.” Then two comparisons: when it comes, it is like a spring dream — how long can that last? When it goes, it is like morning cloud, gone without a trace. The poet never says what “it” is, so readers have guessed for centuries: dew or frost in the night, a brief love affair, or every lovely thing in life that cannot be held. 朝云 (“morning cloud”) also recalls the old legend of the goddess of Mount Wu, who was “morning cloud by day and rain by night” after a night with a king — which is why many read it as a love poem. The lines alternate between three and seven characters, giving it the light rhythm of a song, and its pattern later became a tune name for song lyrics. Its charm lies in never being pinned down: every reader can fill it with something of their own that slipped away.
background: Bai Juyi (772–846) wrote in many forms, from long ballads to tiny songs like this one. Its date and occasion are unknown; it was included among his “miscellaneous songs” and later became a tune pattern for ci lyrics.
pronunciation: 朝云 zhāo（早晨），不读 cháo；几多时 jǐ。
version: 采用通行文本，各版本基本无异文。体裁上它是长短句的杂言诗，后人用它的格式填词，“花非花”成了词牌名。

lines.py: huā fēi huā, wù fēi wù
lines.lit: A flower, not a flower; mist, not mist.
lines.en: A flower that is no flower, a mist that is no mist —

lines.py: yè bàn lái, tiān míng qù
lines.lit: At midnight it comes; at daybreak it goes.
lines.en: it comes at midnight and is gone by dawn.

lines.py: lái rú chūn mèng jǐ duō shí
lines.lit: It comes like a spring dream — how much time?
lines.en: It comes like a spring dream — how long can it stay?

lines.py: qù sì zhāo yún wú mì chù
lines.lit: It goes like morning cloud, with no place to seek it.
lines.en: It leaves like morning cloud, and nowhere can it be found.

words.note: 现代汉语说“不是”；“是非”“非常”里还有这个字。
比喻短暂美好、很快消失的事；成语“春梦一场”。
现代汉语说“多长时间”“多久”。
“朝”读 zhāo，早晨；暗用巫山神女“旦为朝云”的典故。
“觅”= 找；现代汉语说“找不到”。

imagery.name: 花
imagery.zh: 像花又不是花：美好、短暂，又说不清是什么。
imagery.en: Like a flower but not one: lovely, brief, and impossible to name.

imagery.name: 云
imagery.zh: 早晨的云一散就找不到了，比喻美好的东西来去无踪；也暗用巫山神女的爱情传说。
imagery.en: Morning cloud vanishes without a trace — a lovely thing that leaves no sign; it also hints at the legend of the goddess of Mount Wu.
